character_map.blurb: In June 1979, a corporate expedition to the Congolese rainforest is annihilated near the ruins of the Lost City of Zinj. Earth Resources Technology Services dispatches a new team — a mathematical prodigy, a primatologist, a sign-language gorilla, and a mercenary guide — to recover rare Type IIb diamonds and solve the massacre. What they find is a species of grey, hybrid primates bred by an ancient civilization to guard the mines forever.
character_map.notes: Character map based on the 1980 Knopf first edition of Congo by Michael Crichton. All character names verified against Wikipedia (Congo novel article), the official michaelcrichton.com synopsis, Barnes & Noble novel excerpt, the-book-lovers fandom wiki, schoolworkhelper.net, and Books & Boots critical review. The grey gorillas are treated as a collective faction-character per Rule 5 as they have no individual names in canon. Homolka is a film-only named character and is excluded from the novel map.
character_map.title: Congo

factions.label: ERTS (Earth Resources Technology Services)
factions.description: A Houston-based corporate intelligence and resource-extraction firm that treats scientific data as a competitive weapon. Funds the second Congo expedition primarily to secure the diamond contract, subordinating the safety of its field personnel to commercial advantage.

factions.label: Academic Primatology (San Francisco)
factions.description: Peter Elliot's university research circle, focused on primate language acquisition. Drawn into the expedition through Amy's anomalous drawings, representing scientific curiosity in tension with ERTS's purely extractive agenda.

factions.label: Mercenary & Field Guides
factions.description: Charles Munro and his Kikuyu porters: experienced operators who navigate the Congo's political and physical dangers for pay, loyal to the expedition only as long as the contract holds.

factions.label: Euro-Japanese Consortium
factions.description: A rival industrial coalition of German, Japanese, and Dutch interests racing ERTS to the Zinj diamond deposit. Arrives at Zinj first and is entirely destroyed by the grey gorillas before the ERTS party arrives.

factions.label: Grey Gorillas of Zinj
factions.description: A purpose-bred primate species — gorilla/chimpanzee/human hybrids — engineered by the ancient Zinjians to guard the diamond mines. The true antagonists of the novel, revealed at the climax to be not a natural species but a biological weapon of territorial control.

factions.label: Kigani Warriors
factions.description: A hostile local tribe encountered during the expedition's flight from the erupting volcano, representing the human dangers of the Congo's civil-war-torn interior alongside the supernatural threat of the grey gorillas.

character_map.subtitle: Michael Crichton, 1980

characters.name: Dr. Karen Ross
characters.role: ERTS Congo Project Supervisor; field leader of the second expedition
characters.description: A 24-year-old mathematical prodigy whose corporate loyalty and obsessive data-driven planning repeatedly endanger the team — most critically when she detonates explosive charges inside an active volcano to extract diamonds, triggering the eruption that buries Zinj. Her competence is real but instrumentalized entirely in service of ERTS's commercial contract rather than the survival of her colleagues.
characters.name_evidence: Named on michaelcrichton.com official synopsis and Wikipedia as Congo Project Supervisor

characters.name: Dr. Peter Elliot
characters.role: Primatologist; Amy's handler and linguistic interpreter
characters.description: A San Francisco academic whose genuine affection for Amy and scientific integrity make him the expedition's moral centre, yet his professional ego — he intends to name the new hybrid species after himself — reveals the same acquisitive impulse he nominally opposes in ERTS. His ability to translate Amy's communication with the grey gorillas ultimately saves the survivors.
characters.name_evidence: Named on michaelcrichton.com official synopsis and Wikipedia as primatologist and Amy's trainer

characters.name: Amy
characters.role: Sign-language gorilla; unwitting guide to Zinj; interspecies diplomat
characters.description: A female gorilla with a 620-sign vocabulary whose fingerpainted dreams of Zinj initiate the entire expedition; she is both the novel's most sympathetic character and its most instrumentalized — recruited by ERTS as a navigational asset and used by Elliot as a translator with the grey gorillas. In the epilogue she is released into the wild and observed teaching her offspring sign language.
characters.name_evidence: Named on michaelcrichton.com official synopsis; modeled on real gorilla Koko per Crichton's own notes

characters.name: Charles Travis
characters.role: South African mercenary and expedition guide
characters.description: A pragmatic, cynical 'white hunter' in the Allan Quatermain tradition, whose deep knowledge of the Congo's terrain and politics keeps the expedition alive through parachute drops, civil-war crossfire, and Kigani attacks. His pragmatism is the expedition's survival mechanism, though he profits personally — selling recovered diamonds to Intel in the epilogue.
characters.name_evidence: Named on Wikipedia, the-book-lovers fandom wiki, and schoolworkhelper.net as the mercenary guide

characters.name: R.B. Travis
characters.role: Head of ERTS; Karen Ross's superior and the expedition's corporate sponsor
characters.description: The business-driven director of ERTS who frames the entire Congo operation as a race to secure a mineral contract, treating field personnel as expendable assets. His maxim — that the easiest way to obtain information is to steal it — encapsulates the novel's critique of corporate resource extraction dressed as scientific exploration.
characters.name_evidence: Named in Barnes & Noble excerpt and Wikipedia as head of ERTS; full initials confirmed in novel text

characters.name: Gorilla
characters.role: Engineered primate guardians of the Zinj diamond mines; true antagonists
characters.description: Not a natural species but gorilla/chimpanzee/human hybrids bred by the ancient Zinjians as territorial mine-guards — highly aggressive, partially nocturnal, and organized in troops of over a hundred. Their existence is the novel's central mystery and its climactic revelation: the 'monster' is a product of human engineering, not wilderness.
characters.name_evidence: Described throughout novel and on Wikipedia as the primary antagonists; Villains Wiki confirms collective unnamed status

characters.name: Jan Kruger
characters.role: Traveller manning the first expedition's satellite relay; early victim
characters.description: A minor field operative whose night-time encounter with something 'wheezing in the darkness' near the Place of Bones serves as the novel's atmospheric prologue, establishing the grey gorillas' threat before the main expedition begins.
characters.name_evidence: Named in the-book-lovers fandom wiki plot summary as the traveller manning the satellite dish at the 'Place of Bones'

characters.name: Ghost Tribe Member (Uncredited)
characters.role: Rival industrial expedition racing ERTS to Zinj; collectively destroyed by the grey gorillas
characters.description: A large, well-funded coalition of German, Japanese, and Dutch industrial interests who arrive at Zinj ahead of the ERTS party and are entirely annihilated by the grey gorillas — their destroyed camp serving as the ERTS team's first direct evidence of the guardians' lethality.
characters.name_evidence: Described collectively on Wikipedia and michaelcrichton.com as the rival Euro-Japanese industrial expedition

characters.name: Kigani Warriors
characters.role: Hostile local tribe; final human obstacle during the volcanic escape
characters.description: Cannibalistic warriors encountered during the expedition's desperate flight from the erupting Mount Mukenko, representing the human dangers of the Congo's civil-war interior as a counterpoint to the preternatural threat of the grey gorillas.
characters.name_evidence: Named in the-book-lovers fandom wiki and Books & Boots review as the hostile tribe encountered during the escape

character_map.coverage_note: Herkermer Homolka appears in the 1995 film as a named character (Tim Curry) but is not a named character in the novel — the novel's rival-expedition threat is the collective unnamed Consortium. Jan Kruger's fate (death vs. survival) is ambiguous in secondary sources; he is listed as deceased based on contextual evidence from the prologue. The Kikuyu porters who accompany Munro are named collectively in some sources but no individual names were confirmed across authoritative sources and are therefore omitted.

relationships.label: Field agent reporting to corporate director; Travis withholds field command from Ross citing her youth, then deploys her when expedient
Ross recruits Elliot as a primate expert asset; their relationship is defined by competing priorities — her diamond contract vs. his scientific and protective obligations to Amy
Trainer and subject; Elliot's genuine affection for Amy coexists with his use of her as a research instrument and, later, an interspecies translator
Ross hires Munro in Tangiers as expedition guide; their authority clashes repeatedly, most critically over the decision to blast the volcano
Pragmatic mutual reliance in the field; Munro's survival expertise complements Elliot's scientific knowledge of primate behaviour
Amy refers to the grey gorillas as 'bad gorillas'; she serves as the only interspecies communicator capable of transmitting a deterrent message to them
Corporate race to Zinj; the Consortium's head start and data-theft ('piggyback slurp') drive ERTS's frantic pace throughout the expedition
The Consortium expedition arrives at Zinj first and is entirely destroyed by the grey gorillas before the ERTS party reaches the city
The grey gorillas mount repeated nocturnal assaults on the ERTS camp at Zinj; repelled by tear gas, floodlights, and ultimately Amy's translated deterrent broadcast
Kigani warriors pursue the survivors during the volcanic escape; Munro leads the defence while the party commandeers the Consortium's plane

character_map.adaptation_note: The 1995 film (dir. Frank Marshall) substantially restructures the novel: Travis becomes a tech CEO whose son led the first expedition (creating a personal stakes subplot absent from the book), Homolka is invented as a named Romanian philanthropist villain killed by the grey gorillas at the mine, and Karen destroys Travis's satellite in a final act of corporate rebellion that has no equivalent in Crichton's novel. The book's ending — escape by hot-air balloon, Munro selling diamonds to Intel, Amy released to the wild — is broadly retained but the film adds the laser-weapon set piece and omits the novel's epilogue.
character_map.setting_preamble: ERTS (Earth Resources Technology Services) is a Houston-based corporation that treats geographic and biological data as proprietary commodities, funding expeditions to secure rare industrial resources before rival consortia. The Lost City of Zinj is a fictional ruined city in the Virunga volcanic region of the eastern Congo, source of Type IIb boron-doped blue diamonds valuable as semiconductors. The grey gorillas guarding Zinj are not a natural species but a purpose-bred hybrid — gorilla, chimpanzee, and possibly human — engineered by Zinj's ancient inhabitants as living mine-guards, a fact unknown to any expedition until the novel's climax.
